title: Which button reaches floor minus five from other floors?
description: The lift must stop on floor minus five from different starting floors. The floors between the start and the target are counted, and the direction gives plus or minus. One ride is checked by counting.
teaching_notes: One idea: the button depends on the starting floor, so one target has many correct rides. Watch for students who press minus five from every start.

video_script.why: The child finds the button that takes the lift from a chosen starting floor to a fixed target floor below the ground.
video_script.substitution: the book's own target floor minus five, with several starting floors
video_script.anchor: the lift in {{NAME_10}}, trying to reach floor minus five from different floors
video_script.payoff_line: Different starting floors need different buttons to reach the same target floor.

final_answer.spoken: from plus one press minus six, from minus two press minus three, from zero press minus five, and from minus six press plus one

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: the button is always minus five
maths_rules: Starting Floor + Movement = Target Floor, with the target −5.
(+2) + (−7) = −5 is the example in the book.
video_script.design: One idea: count the floors from any start to the target. One lift picture throughout. Method as in the solved example. The question is open-ended, so the video shows four of many correct rides.
open_questions: The question is open-ended; the video shows four example rides and the board answer for the child lists any valid ones.

beats.on_screen: title card Reach Minus Five; the lift of the tall block appears with the target floor minus five marked below the ground

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the lift appears
marks.target: floor minus five is outlined below the ground floor
marks.ask: the question is written into the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='target'/>The lift must reach floor minus five, which is below the ground.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Starting from different floors, which button must you press each time?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the lift beside a floor line with the target floor minus five outlined; an up arrow and a down arrow are drawn, and the example start plus two is tagged

marks.count: the floors between a start and the target are bracketed
marks.way: the solved example from the book is shown beside the lift
marks.dir: the up arrow is tagged plus and the down arrow is tagged minus

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>The button depends on how many floors lie between the start and the target.
<bookmark mark='way'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='dir'/>If the target is lower, press minus. If it is higher, press plus.

beats.on_screen: Given: the target is Floor −5; the example starts at +2 and presses −7

marks.given: the line Given is written on the working board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the lift must stop on floor minus five.
The example in your book starts on plus two, and presses minus seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the button for other starting floors that also reach −5

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find buttons for other starting floors that also reach minus five.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the example, from +2 go down 7 floors to −5, press −7: (+2) + (−7) = −5

marks.ex: the example start plus two is circled
marks.seven: the lift drops seven floors from plus two to minus five

narration: <bookmark mark='ex'/>Step one, see how the example works.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>From plus two, the lift goes down seven floors, so the press is minus seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: start +1, 1 floor to 0 and 5 more floors, 6 floors down, press −6: (+1) + (−6) = −5

marks.start: floor plus one is tagged as the new start
marks.cross: the lift drops one floor to the ground and five more floors to minus five

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step two, start from plus one.
<bookmark mark='cross'/>One floor reaches the ground, and five more floors reach minus five.
Six floors down means the press is minus six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: start −2, 3 floors down, press −3: (−2) + (−3) = −5; start 0, 5 floors down, press −5: 0 + (−5) = −5

marks.two: floor minus two is tagged and the lift drops three floors
marks.zero: the ground floor is tagged and the lift drops five floors

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, start from minus two.
Minus two to minus five is three floors down, so the press is minus three.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>From the ground floor, it is five floors down, so the press is minus five.

marks.low: floor minus six is tagged under the target floor
marks.up: the lift rises one floor to minus five

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step four, start from minus six, which is below the target.
<bookmark mark='up'/>Minus five is one floor up, so the press is plus one.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check the start +1, count 6 floors down: 0, −1, −2, −3, −4, −5

marks.check: the lift drops from plus one floor by floor
marks.land: each of the six floors is lit and minus five is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the start of plus one by counting six floors down.
<bookmark mark='land'/>Zero, minus one, minus two, minus three, minus four, and then minus five.

marks.ans: the answer lines are boxed on the working board
marks.pay: the four rides are shown ending on the same floor

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>From plus one press minus six, and from minus two press minus three.
From zero press minus five, and from minus six press plus one.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Different starting floors need different buttons to reach the same target floor.
